# 01 Load

## Purpose

Load the raw GSE7904 expression data and sample metadata. Record the source, platform and initial checks.

## Input / Output

| Type | File |
|:--|:--|
| **Reads** | `data/_raw/GSE7904_series_matrix.txt.gz` |
| **Writes** | `data/01_dat_load.tsv` |
| **Writes** | `data/01_sample_metadata.tsv` |


## Data provenance

### Dataset identification

The expression data used in this project originate from the
Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database, maintained by the
National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI).

- **GEO accession:** GSE7904
- **Study title:** Expression data from human breast tissue
- **Organism:** Homo sapiens
- **GEO platform:** GPL570
- **Measurement technology:** Affymetrix microarray

Original dataset:
https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE7904

### Platform and measurement information

The dataset was generated using the Affymetrix Human Genome
U133 Plus 2.0 Array (GPL570).

The imported expression measurements are identified in the
GEO Series Matrix file as dChip signal values.

These measurements are preserved as provided in the GEO
Series Matrix file. No additional logarithmic transformation
or normalization is performed during the data-loading step.

### Download information

The original GEO Series Matrix file is downloaded from NCBI
and stored in the project's `data/_raw/` directory.

- **Source file:** GSE7904_series_matrix.txt.gz
- **File format:** Compressed tab-delimited text
- **Download URL:**
  https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE7nnn/GSE7904/matrix/GSE7904_series_matrix.txt.gz

The downloaded source file is preserved unchanged.
Its MD5 checksum is calculated to support file integrity
verification.

### Dataset composition

The imported dataset contains:

- 62 biological samples
- 54,675 Affymetrix probe identifiers
- 43 tumour samples
- 7 normal breast samples
- 12 normal organelle samples

The tumour samples include Basal, non-BLC and BRCA1
characteristics.

The normal breast and normal organelle samples are retained
as separate biological groups.


## Setup

```{r}

#| label: 01_setup
#| message: false

# Load required packages
library(tidyverse)
library(here)

# Identify the project root directory
project_root <- here::here()

# Define the data directories
raw_dir <- here::here("data", "_raw")
data_dir <- here::here("data")

# Create the directories if they do not already exist.
# This is important because Git does not include the ignored data/ folder.
dir.create(data_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(raw_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Display project information
cat("Project root:", project_root, "\n")
cat("Raw data directory:", raw_dir, "\n")
cat("Data directory:", data_dir, "\n")
```

## Load data

```{r}

#| label: 01_load-data
#| message: false

# GEO accession and download URL
geo_accession <- "GSE7904"

geo_url <- paste0(
  "https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE7nnn/",
  geo_accession,
  "/matrix/",
  geo_accession,
  "_series_matrix.txt.gz"
)

# Define the destination of the original file
series_matrix_file <- file.path(
  raw_dir,
  paste0(geo_accession, "_series_matrix.txt.gz")
)

# Download the file only if it does not already exist
if (!file.exists(series_matrix_file)) {

  download.file(
    url = geo_url,
    destfile = series_matrix_file,
    mode = "wb",
    method = "libcurl"
  )

}

# Verify that the downloaded file exists and is not empty
if (!file.exists(series_matrix_file) ||
    file.info(series_matrix_file)$size == 0) {
  stop("The GEO Series Matrix file was not downloaded correctly.")
}

# Report file information
cat("Download successful!\n")
cat("File:", series_matrix_file, "\n")
cat("File size:", round(file.info(series_matrix_file)$size / 1024^2, 2), "MB\n")

# Calculate an MD5 checksum for provenance
cat("MD5 checksum:\n")
print(tools::md5sum(series_matrix_file))

```

## Initial checks and data import

```{r}

#| label: 01_inspect-source
#| message: false

# Open the compressed GEO file and read its contents
geo_connection <- gzfile(series_matrix_file, open = "rt")
geo_lines <- readLines(geo_connection, warn = FALSE)
close(geo_connection)

# Display the first 35 lines to inspect the file structure
cat(head(geo_lines, 35), sep = "\n")

```




```{r}

#| label: 01_import-metadata
#| message: false

# Reusable function: find one GEO metadata row and return
# its values for all samples (excluding the field-name column).
extract_sample_field <- function(field_name) {

  line_index <- which(startsWith(geo_lines, field_name))

  if (length(line_index) == 0) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Read the metadata line as tab-separated data
  parsed <- read.delim(
    text = geo_lines[line_index[1]],
    header = FALSE,
    sep = "\t",
    quote = "\"",
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  as.character(unlist(parsed[1, -1], use.names = FALSE))
}

# Extract sample identifiers, titles and source descriptions.
# These vectors are combined below to create one row per sample.
sample_ids <- extract_sample_field("!Sample_geo_accession")
sample_titles <- extract_sample_field("!Sample_title")
sample_sources <- extract_sample_field("!Sample_source_name_ch1")

# Find all GEO rows containing sample characteristics.
# Each row can describe a different characteristic for the samples.
characteristic_indices <- which(
  startsWith(geo_lines, "!Sample_characteristics_ch1")
)

characteristics <- lapply(characteristic_indices, function(i) {

  parsed <- read.delim(
    text = geo_lines[i],
    header = FALSE,
    sep = "\t",
    quote = "\"",
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  as.character(unlist(parsed[1, -1], use.names = FALSE))
})

# Create the metadata table
sample_metadata <- tibble(
  sample_id = sample_ids,
  sample_title = sample_titles,
  sample_source = sample_sources
)

# Add each characteristics row as a separate metadata column.
# characteristic_1, for example, contains the first GEO characteristic
# for every sample; it is not a count of characteristics.
for (i in seq_along(characteristics)) {
  sample_metadata[[paste0("characteristic_", i)]] <-
    characteristics[[i]]
}

# Remove temporary extraction objects that are no longer needed
rm(characteristic_indices, characteristics)

# Inspect the result
dim(sample_metadata)
head(sample_metadata)

```

```{r}

#| label: 01_import-expression
#| message: false

# Find the lines marking the beginning and end of the expression matrix
table_begin <- grep("^!series_matrix_table_begin", geo_lines)
table_end <- grep("^!series_matrix_table_end", geo_lines)

# Check that both markers were found exactly once and in the correct order
if (length(table_begin) != 1 ||
    length(table_end) != 1 ||
    table_begin >= table_end) {
  stop("Could not identify the expression matrix boundaries in the GEO file.")
}

# Display the positions of the markers
cat("Expression matrix begins at line:", table_begin, "\n")
cat("Expression matrix ends at line:", table_end, "\n")

# Extract the lines containing the expression matrix
expression_lines <- geo_lines[
  (table_begin + 1):(table_end - 1)
]

# Import the expression matrix
expression_data <- read.delim(
  text = paste(expression_lines, collapse = "\n"),
  header = TRUE,
  sep = "\t",
  quote = "\"",
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  na.strings = c("", "NA")
)

# Remove the temporary text vector; the imported data is now in expression_data
rm(expression_lines)

# Inspect the imported expression data
dim(expression_data)
head(expression_data[, 1:6])
str(expression_data[, 1:6])

```

```{r}

#| label: 01_check-dimensions
#| message: false

# Check the complete dataset dimensions
cat("Expression matrix dimensions:\n")
print(dim(expression_data))

cat("\nSample metadata dimensions:\n")
print(dim(sample_metadata))

# Count how many samples belong to each original GEO category
cat("\nNumber of samples in each original GEO category:\n")
print(
  sample_metadata %>%
    count(characteristic_1, sort = TRUE)
)

# Inspect all sample titles and classifications
print(
  sample_metadata %>%
    select(sample_id, sample_title, characteristic_1),
  n = Inf
)

```

```{r}

#| label: 01_check-expression-values
#| message: false

# Calculate basic expression statistics
expression_values <- unlist(expression_data[-1], use.names = FALSE)

summary(expression_values)

cat("\nMinimum expression value:", min(expression_values), "\n")
cat("Maximum expression value:", max(expression_values), "\n")
cat("Mean expression value:", mean(expression_values), "\n")
cat("Standard deviation:", sd(expression_values), "\n")

# Remove the temporary vector to keep the R environment cleaner
rm(expression_values)

```

```{r}

#| label: 01_classify-samples
#| message: false

# Assign each sample to its biological tissue group
sample_metadata <- sample_metadata %>%
  mutate(
    tissue_group = case_when(
      characteristic_1 %in% c("Basal", "non-BLC", "BRCA1") ~ "Tumour",
      characteristic_1 == "NB" ~ "Normal breast",
      characteristic_1 == "NO" ~ "Normal organelle",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# Check whether every sample received a classification
if (any(is.na(sample_metadata$tissue_group))) {
  stop("Some samples could not be assigned to a tissue group.")
}

# Display the resulting group sizes
sample_metadata %>%
  count(tissue_group, sort = TRUE)

```


```{r}

#| label: 01_validate-data
#| message: false

# Check the number of samples in both objects
cat("Samples in metadata:", nrow(sample_metadata), "\n")
cat("Samples in expression matrix:", ncol(expression_data) - 1, "\n")

# Check whether sample IDs match
expression_sample_ids <- colnames(expression_data)[-1]

cat(
  "All expression samples have metadata:",
  all(expression_sample_ids %in% sample_metadata$sample_id),
  "\n"
)

cat(
  "All metadata samples have expression data:",
  all(sample_metadata$sample_id %in% expression_sample_ids),
  "\n"
)

# Check for duplicated probe identifiers
cat(
  "Duplicated probe IDs:",
  sum(duplicated(expression_data$ID_REF)),
  "\n"
)

# Check for missing expression values
cat(
  "Missing expression values:",
  sum(is.na(expression_data[-1])),
  "\n"
)

```


## Save output

```{r}

#| label: 01_save
#| message: false

# Define output file paths
expression_output <- here::here("data", "01_dat_load.tsv")
metadata_output <- here::here("data", "01_sample_metadata.tsv")

# Save expression matrix
readr::write_tsv(
  expression_data,
  expression_output
)

# Save sample metadata
readr::write_tsv(
  sample_metadata,
  metadata_output
)

# Confirm that both files were created
if (!file.exists(expression_output) ||
    !file.exists(metadata_output)) {
  stop("One or more output files could not be created.")
}

cat("Output files successfully saved:\n")
cat(expression_output, "\n")
cat(metadata_output, "\n")

```

## Final validation

```{r}

#| label: 01_final-validation
#| message: false

# Read the saved files back into R
saved_expression <- readr::read_tsv(
  expression_output,
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

saved_metadata <- readr::read_tsv(
  metadata_output,
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# Check dimensions
stopifnot(
  identical(dim(saved_expression), dim(expression_data)),
  identical(dim(saved_metadata), dim(sample_metadata))
)

# Check sample identifiers
stopifnot(
  identical(
    colnames(saved_expression)[-1],
    saved_metadata$sample_id
  )
)

# Check tissue group counts
print(saved_metadata %>% count(tissue_group))

# Confirm successful validation
cat("\nAll saved output validation checks passed!\n")

```
